evidence: Type inventory of the frozen task (hashes re-verified against manifest: functional judge.toml 317d8204..., polish 6b4a88ca..., visual 35e075aa..., visual prompt.md 18d64251..., scoring.toml 95f70d6e...). GATES: tests/gates/render/judge.toml:19-23 hro_gate_render type=binary and tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:19-23 hro_gate_shared type=binary, both aggregation all_pass; gate criteria are pass/fail (sign-in works; server-backed save visible in independent context), so binary is required and correct (deterministic-checks.md:42). FUNCTIONAL: all 12 criteria binary (functional/judge.toml lines 28,37,46,55,64,73,82,91,100,109,118,127). Each is a pass/fail behavioural bar: stage-move legality, 409 stale refusal, capacity refusal, bulk atomicity, undo refusal, role 403/401/404 replays, message escaping/Enter/Shift+Enter, 30-message paging, unread/seen counts, candidate data leakage. None is a degree-of-quality judgement; thresholds such as 'within 15 seconds' are crisp binary cut-offs. POLISH: all 5 criteria binary (polish/judge.toml:22,31,40,49,58): draft/focus/scroll preservation under a live update (within 2 px), earlier-messages anchor, failed-send explanation+no duplicate, ended-session re-auth and per-user draft isolation. These are behavioural preservation checks with observable yes/no outcomes, not craft, so binary fits; the template's own polish dimension is also all-binary (template polish/judge.toml: responsive_layout, accessible_controls, interaction_feedback, workspace_coherence). VISUAL (the craft dimension): all 5 criteria type=likert, points=5 (visual/judge.toml:22-23,37-38,52-53,67-68,82-83), and every one has a described anchor at each level 5,4,3,2,1 (e.g. hro_vis_type lines 27-31; hro_vis_color 42-46; hro_vis_layout 57-61; hro_vis_hierarchy 72-76; hro_vis_consistency 87-91). This matches the shipped template format (template visual/judge.toml uses likert points=5 with anchors). The task uses 1-5 anchors (template also lists a 0 anchor); with points=5 a 1-5 scale is internally consistent, and the visual prompt.md:12 and :20 define the minimum as 'raw Likert score 1, which normalizes to zero', and prompt.md:7 'lowest score (binary 0; Likert 1)' — the minimum is consistently defined in prompt and anchors, so no out-of-range 0 can be requested. INTERNAL ANNOTATION: the workbook note says practice is 'binary and weighted, Likert we dont use in rewardkit'; per SKILL.md:65 and quality-checks.md:170 this is a known false positive — judged against the shipped format, the presence of likert in visual is not a defect. Weighted binary is used throughout functional/polish as the note describes. COLDERWATER LESSONS checked for this row: L4 (keep gates simple) — gates are single binary criteria; L6 checker-not-fixer — every prompt maps a non-working feature to 'binary 0; Likert 1', consistent with each dimension's type; L2 (weights) — not this row; per-type weights are documented (visual equal at 1, comment line 17). Adversarial tries: (a) a broken app that could pass this row's concern — an app with poor visuals cannot gain binary craft credit because no craft item is binary; an app with dead behaviour cannot earn graded partial credit for a pass/fail behaviour because all behaviours are binary. (b) a conforming alternative that could fail — an app with an unconventional but coherent visual style is graded on described 1-5 anchors that do not prescribe a specific style (prompt.md:14 'Layout, labels and styles are the implementer's choice'), so it is not forced to a binary fail. Minor observation (not a defect for row 41): visual prompt.md:18 says 'A step you skipped or did differently fails that criterion' — 'fails' is binary wording in a likert dimension, but :12/:20 and :7 resolve the minimum as Likert 1, so the outcome is defined. Bundling many legs into large conjunctive binaries (e.g. hro_moves weight 7) affects gradation/discrimination (rows 26/40), not the binary-vs-likert type fit assessed here. No runtime measurement is required to judge type fit; RewardKit's actual likert normalization was not executed by this reviewer (score.py is template-identical, hash 13de2b38...).
